questions.q: You must check quickly whether a transaction id has already been processed, and order does not matter. Which collection fits best?
o: `HashSet`, with O(1) average `contains`
`ArrayList`, scanning with `contains`
`LinkedList`, scanning from the head
`PriorityQueue`, peeking at the head
questions.w: A set answers membership questions. `ArrayList.contains` is O(n), so a loop over many ids becomes O(n²).

questions.q: What happens when `ArrayList` is full and you call `add`?
o: It allocates a larger array (about 1.5×) and copies the elements
It throws an `IllegalStateException` for a full list
It links a new node to the end of the list
It overwrites the oldest element in the array
questions.w: The copy is O(n) but rare, so appending is amortised O(1). Pre-size with `new ArrayList<>(n)` when you know the size.

questions.q: A for-each loop over a list calls `list.remove(item)` inside the body. What is the usual result?
o: `ConcurrentModificationException` on the next iteration
The item is removed and the loop continues normally
A `NullPointerException` from the iterator
The loop restarts from the first element
questions.w: The iterator's expected `modCount` no longer matches. Use `removeIf` or `Iterator.remove()` instead.

questions.q: What does `PriorityQueue` guarantee about iteration order?
o: Nothing useful: only `poll` returns elements in priority order
Elements come out sorted from smallest to largest
Elements come out in insertion order
Elements come out in reverse sorted order
questions.w: It is a binary heap. The head is the smallest, but the rest of the array is only partially ordered. Poll repeatedly to get sorted output.

questions.q: Which is the best choice for a stack or a simple FIFO queue in single-threaded code?
o: `ArrayDeque`
`Stack`
`LinkedList`
`Vector`
questions.w: `ArrayDeque` is a circular array with O(1) at both ends and no node overhead. `Stack` and `Vector` are legacy synchronized classes.

questions.q: `Collections.unmodifiableList(list)` is returned from a method. The owner later adds an element to `list`. What does the caller see?
o: The new element, because the wrapper is only a read-only view
The old contents, because the wrapper copied the list
An `UnsupportedOperationException` on the next read
An empty list, because the wrapper was invalidated
questions.w: An unmodifiable wrapper blocks changes through itself, not through the original. `List.copyOf` makes an independent immutable snapshot.

questions.q: A `TreeSet<BigDecimal>` receives `new BigDecimal("1.0")` and then `new BigDecimal("1.00")`. How many elements does it hold?
o: One, because `compareTo` treats them as equal
Two, because `equals` treats them as different
Zero, because both values are rejected
Two, because the scale is different
questions.w: `TreeSet` uses `compareTo`, which ignores scale. A `HashSet` uses `equals`, which does not, so it would keep both.

questions.q: What is a safe, idiomatic way to remove duplicates from a list while keeping first-seen order?
o: `new ArrayList<>(new LinkedHashSet<>(list))`
`new ArrayList<>(new HashSet<>(list))`
`new ArrayList<>(new TreeSet<>(list))`
`Collections.unmodifiableList(list)`
questions.w: `HashSet` loses order and `TreeSet` sorts. `LinkedHashSet` removes duplicates and remembers insertion order. `stream().distinct()` also works.
